Dr Robins 
Head of Orthopaedic Ward
St Peter’s Hospital
Birmingham

25 October 2019

Dear Dr Robins

Re: Mr Sydney Cherry
DOB: 17/04/1947

Thank you for seeing Mr Sydney Cherry, a 73-year-old gentleman who has an exacerbation of chronic osteoarthritis, for which he requires a surgical intervention.

Mr Cherry has had osteoarthritis since 2007 and hypertension since 2013, for which he takes Panadol Osteo and Co-tenidone, respectively. He received multiple physiotherapy sessions to manage the knee pain and sciatica. He is physically active, and currently lives alone.

Mr Cherry first presented on 03/03/2019 complaining of progressive bilateral knee joint pain prodominantly in the rigth knee. The was tenderness along with restricted movement in the right knee.He was condequently prescribed naproxen 250 mg twice daily. 

Three weeks later, an X-ray of the rigth knee detected signs of severe osteoarthritis with the presence of osteophytes and loss of joint space. Therefore,  physiotherapy sessions were stated with an adjustment of the analgesia. 

Despite having treatment, Mr Cherry’s condition further deteriorated. On 07/07/2019, he reported experiencing pain at rest after walking.He was counseled on having a knee replacement, and today he agreed. 

Please note, an arthroplasty has been scheduled for the 20th of November, and Mr Cherry will be admitted to hospital the day before. 

It would be greatly appreciated if you could take Mr Cherry into your care.

Yours sincerely

Doctor.
